title: Discovery call with Marcus
body: Marcus walked through current onboarding. New consumer accounts take about 3 days end to end and roughly a third of online applications are abandoned before completion. Branch staff re-key ID data into the core and manual KYC review queues back up on Mondays. He wants to cut time to open to same day. Agreed to a technical workshop with core systems.

title: Core-systems integration workshop
body: Session with Tobias and his team on how Ledgerline connects to their core banking platform. Concerns: real-time vs batch posting, how failed account creations are rolled back, and middleware ownership. Tobias wants a reference architecture and sandbox test before he signs off. Marcus sat in and pushed for a phased rollout starting with checking.

title: Sent integration reference architecture
body: Sent Tobias the reference architecture, API rate limits and the sandbox access request form. Flagged the rollback pattern he asked about for failed core account creation.

title: Call with Marcus and compliance officer
body: Priyanka joined for the first time. Skeptical about automated decisioning on KYC exceptions and wants to see how every decision is logged. Asked for the audit-trail documentation and a BSA/AML evidence pack covering CIP, OFAC screening and SAR escalation handoffs. She wants nothing that reduces examiner visibility. Committed to send the pack within a week.

title: Sent audit-trail and BSA/AML evidence pack
body: Sent Priyanka the audit-trail overview, sample exam-ready decision log and BSA/AML control mapping. Offered a walkthrough with our compliance lead.

title: Security questionnaire returned
body: Completed security questionnaire sent back to Tobias's team. Covered SOC 2 report, encryption, data residency and vendor access controls. Two follow-up questions on pen test scope; answered same day. No red flags so far.

title: Budget confirmation with Marcus
body: Marcus confirmed the $240K is approved in this year's operations budget. Main remaining risk is Priyanka's sign-off. He suggested keeping the compliance review focused on exception handling and examiner reporting. Close targeted within the next month.

title: Prep compliance review demo of exception queue
body: Build a short demo of the exception queue and audit log export with sample BSA/AML flags. Confirm our compliance lead can attend.

title: Compliance review meeting
body: Review with Priyanka and Marcus. Walk through exception workflows, decision logging and examiner reporting using the evidence pack. Bring our compliance lead. Goal: get her conditions for approval in writing.

title: Referral received from peer credit union
body: Referral came in from a CU in Utah that went live with us last year. Their ops lead said onboarding dropped from about 25 minutes to under 8. Odalys at Fernhollow is expecting our outreach. Their issue: members under 35 abandon the in-branch process and the web form.

title: Intro email to Odalys
body: Sent a short intro referencing the referral and offered two times for a discovery call. She replied within a few hours and picked the following week.

title: Discovery call - mobile account opening
body: Odalys says roughly 40% of online applications are abandoned before ID verification. Branch staff re-key data into the core, which takes about 15 minutes per new member. Goal is mobile account opening for members aged 18-34 by next year. Budget is not locked, but she expects to sponsor it. She asked about core integration and mentioned lending will want a say. Next step: demo for her team.

title: Sent recap and security overview
body: Sent the discovery recap, our SOC 2 summary, and a one-page overview of the document and ID verification flow. Asked Odalys to confirm who from her team should attend the demo.

title: Demo for member experience team
body: Walked through mobile account opening, ID capture and automated KYC checks. Six people from member experience and branch ops attended. The team liked the drop-off analytics and the short flow. Odalys said it was the best fit she has seen. Rafferty joined for the last 15 minutes and asked whether we handle loan pre-qualification for new members. He wants to see it before forming a view. Promised a follow-up demo focused on lending.

title: Debrief with Odalys
body: Odalys said the feedback was positive overall. Rafferty is neutral and cares about pre-qualification and how decisions feed the loan origination system. She suggested showing a real member journey from account opening to a pre-approved auto loan offer. She will help get 45 minutes on his calendar.

title: Prep lending-focused demo scenario
body: Build a demo flow: new member opens account on mobile, soft-pull pre-qualification, auto loan offer. Confirm with solutions engineering which loan origination integrations we can show live. Prepare answers on pre-qualification rules and adverse action handling.

title: Follow-up demo: loan pre-qualification
body: Demo for Rafferty and the member experience team focused on pre-qualification and the handoff into the loan origination system. Goal is to get his view on fit and to identify who else on the lending side should review.

title: Discovery follow-up with Delphine
body: Branch onboarding averages 38 minutes per new checking account and she wants it under 15. Asked for a demo focused on joint accounts.

title: Platform demo for ops team
body: Walk through the account-opening flow with six branch managers. Delphine wants to see the paper-form fallback.

title: Sent KYC rules overview
body: Garrett asked how risk scoring thresholds are configured. Sent the doc and offered a call with our compliance engineer.

title: Schedule BSA review call
body: Book a technical call with Garrett and our compliance engineer to cover CIP and watchlist screening.

title: Exec sponsor alignment
body: Imogen confirmed the CEO supports the project. Open question is whether the board loan committee needs a risk summary before signoff.

title: Draft board risk summary
body: Prepare a two-page summary on data retention and vendor oversight for Imogen to bring to the board.

title: Intro to business onboarding module
body: Imogen mentioned business accounts still take about a week to open. Sent a one-pager on beneficial ownership capture.

title: Business lending team intro
body: Initial meeting with the business services manager to map the current account-opening steps.

title: Contract questions
body: Calloway's attorney flagged the data breach notification window. Agreed to take it back to our legal team.

title: Send revised notification clause
body: Get legal's redline on the 72-hour breach clause and send it to Calloway.

title: Pilot declined
body: Calloway said they are freezing new vendor spend until after the core conversion. Agreed to revisit next year.

title: Compliance pain points
body: Lucinda's team manually reviews roughly 400 flagged applications a month. Wants false positives cut by at least a third.

title: Review sample alert data
body: Working session with Lucinda to run anonymized past alerts through our screening logic.

title: Sent integration questionnaire
body: Emeka needs to confirm API access on their core before scoping. Asked for the vendor's API documentation.

title: Follow up on API docs
body: Check whether Emeka received the core provider's API docs and set the technical scoping call.

title: Signed and kickoff planning
body: Winifred signed after the reference call with another bank. Kickoff is set for next month with her ops team.

title: Sent ag lending use case
body: Shared how entity and ownership verification works for farm LLCs. Winifred wants to see it with a partnership example.

title: Ag lending demo
body: Demo for Winifred and two loan officers with a farm partnership scenario.

title: CCO concerns call
body: Bartholomew worries about audit trails for automated decisions. Promised a sample examiner-ready report.

title: Send sample audit report
body: Package an anonymized audit trail export and send to Bartholomew and Saoirse.

title: Lost to incumbent
body: Their mortgage LOS vendor bundled identity checks at no extra cost. Left the door open for the broader onboarding project.

title: Intro call with CEO
body: Ignacia wants members to join without coming into a branch, and many prefer Spanish-language flows. Asked about language support.

title: Spanish-language flow demo
body: Show the bilingual onboarding screens and discuss ID types for members without standard documents.

title: Fraud losses context
body: They lost about 60k last year to synthetic ID account fraud. Ignacia will bring the risk committee into the next conversation.

title: Prepare fraud loss comparison
body: Build a short comparison of expected fraud reduction against the add-on cost.

title: Final terms discussion
body: Lorcan wants a phased rollout by branch cluster. Philippa still needs our SOC 2 report and a subcontractor list.

title: Send SOC 2 and subcontractor list
body: Deliver the vendor risk package to Philippa so she can close out due diligence.

title: Wealth onboarding overview
body: Sent materials on suitability questionnaires inside the account opening flow. Lorcan will loop in the wealth division head.

title: Wealth division presentation
body: Present to the wealth team on e-signature and KYC refresh for existing clients.

title: Order form signed
body: Anselm returned the signed order form. Go-live targeted for next quarter, starting with the two highest-volume branches.

title: Youth accounts scoping
body: Anselm wants a guardian-consent flow for minors. Checking whether our current template handles custodial accounts.

title: Confirm custodial account support
body: Get product's answer on custodial and guardian flows and reply to Anselm.

title: Budget conversation
body: Thessaly is interested but budget is tight until next fiscal year. Wants a pricing option sized for a bank under 100 employees.

title: Pricing walkthrough
body: Review the small-institution tier and expected staff time savings with Thessaly.

title: Decided to stay manual
body: Thessaly said volume of nonprofit accounts is too low to justify the cost right now. Will reconsider if volume grows.

title: Discovery follow-up
body: Nadine says new members wait about 4 days for account approval and abandon 30% of online applications. She wants a demo with the BSA officer in the room.

title: Product demo with BSA team
body: Walk through the KYC decision rules and exception queue with Hollis and two analysts.

title: Intro on business onboarding
body: Sent a one-pager on small-business onboarding after Nadine mentioned they open about 40 business accounts a month by hand.

title: Schedule scoping call
body: Book a 30-minute call to size business document collection needs.

title: Compliance concerns call
body: Mireille wants audit trail samples and a clear answer on how false-positive watchlist hits get escalated. Dorian is pushing to finish by quarter end.

title: Compliance review session
body: Show audit reporting and model governance documentation to Mireille's team.

title: Core vendor check
body: Their core provider charges per API call and Dorian worries about cost. Need pricing clarity from IT before moving on.

title: Send integration architecture doc
body: Send the integration diagram and sample API volumes to their IT director.

title: Contract questions
body: Henrik asked about the termination clause and implementation timeline. Legal is reviewing redlines this week.

title: Send revised order form
body: Return the updated order form with the 90-day go-live commitment.

title: Loss follow-up
body: Henrik chose to hold off on lending workflows until next year because of budget. Agreed to revisit after account opening goes live.

title: Qualification call
body: Juniper has budget approved for this fiscal year and wants identity verification built into the mobile app. Dashiell worries about synthetic identity fraud.

title: Fraud controls workshop
body: Review document and selfie verification options with Dashiell.

title: Signed order confirmation
body: Received signed order for the joint-account module. Kickoff scheduled with their member services lead.

title: Backlog discussion
body: Cordelia has roughly 9,000 customer files overdue for review and four analysts on the team. Wants to see automated refresh outreach.

title: Refresh workflow demo
body: Demo risk-tiered refresh campaigns with her analysts and the head of wealth operations.

title: Intro to wealth team
body: Cordelia introduced the head of wealth operations. Sent a summary of high-net-worth onboarding capabilities.

title: Prep wealth use-case outline
body: Draft a short outline of beneficial ownership and source-of-funds steps for the first meeting.

title: CIO alignment call
body: Weston is on board but wants a security questionnaire answered and proof the platform handles their legacy core without middleware. CFO sign-off is next.

title: Return security questionnaire
body: Complete and send the 120-question vendor security review.

title: Discovery notes
body: Ottoline processes applications by hand with two staff and loses new members to slow turnaround. Board approval needed for anything over 25k.

title: Draft board summary
body: Write a one-page ROI summary for Ottoline to share with the board.

title: Contract sent
body: Sent the agreement after Leopold confirmed budget. Procurement is asking for a SOC 2 report and a data processing addendum.

title: Procurement walkthrough
body: Join a call with procurement to resolve security and insurance requirements.

title: Requirements call
body: Xiomara needs Spanish-language application and document capture, and about 35% of applicants lack a standard utility bill for address proof.

title: Demo of Spanish workflow
body: Show the bilingual flow and alternative address verification options.

title: Loss debrief
body: Barnaby renewed with their incumbent vendor after a discount, though he said integration speed was our edge. Check back in nine months.

title: Discovery follow-up with ops
body: Teodora said new member applications take about 25 minutes in branch and 30% get stuck in manual ID review. Wants to see mobile flow and exception queue.

title: Platform demo for ops and compliance
body: Walk through mobile onboarding and KYC review queue with Teodora and Rhys. Bring a sample audit trail report.

title: Contract review call
body: Caspian is ready to sign but Matilda wants a clause on audit log retention and a sandbox test of the core connector. Legal redlines coming back this week.

title: Send core integration test plan
body: Share the sandbox test plan for the core-banking connector so Matilda can sign off before signature.

title: Intro reply from Fenwick
body: Fenwick replied to our outreach saying paper applications are slowing deposit growth. Agreed to a first call to scope requirements.

title: Intro call
body: 30-minute scoping call on current account-opening steps, core vendor and volume of new accounts per month.

title: Qualification notes
body: Budget approved for this fiscal year, about 1,200 new members a month. Ambrose worried about integration with their older core and wants references.

title: Send integration references
body: Line up two credit union references running on a similar core and send to Ambrose.

title: Decision notice
body: Gideon said they are extending their core provider's onboarding module to avoid a second integration. Asked to reconnect next year.
